metaDescription: Six electric leaf blowers, cordless and corded, compared on air volume, speed settings, weight and battery platform for low-noise yard cleanup.
expertTake: The EGO LB5302 is the best overall pick because its brushless motor and variable dial let you work at a lower, quieter setting and still move a lot of air. The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is the value pick for small yards and is described by its maker as a low-noise design. Anyone clearing wet leaves from a large property should skip quiet electrics and buy a stronger backpack blower.
introParagraphs: Gas leaf blowers are loud because a small two-stroke or four-stroke engine runs near full speed all day. Electric blowers, cordless or corded, are the quieter class, and they also start instantly, produce no exhaust and can be used earlier in the morning or in neighborhoods with noise rules.

Quiet is not the same as weak, but it is a tradeoff. A blower that runs at a lower speed setting makes less noise and moves less air, while a turbo button restores power and the noise with it. This guide compares six electric blowers and explains how to read the volume, speed and battery numbers so you can match the machine to your yard.

products.name: EGO Power+ LB5302 530 CFM Cordless Leaf Blower With Battery
products.description:
The EGO LB5302 uses a brushless motor and a 56V battery to deliver 530 CFM of air, with a variable speed dial and a lock-on button for long sessions. A turbo mode is there for wet leaves and caked grass, but the practical value for noise-conscious owners is the dial: running at a mid setting keeps the sound down while still moving a surprising amount of air. The maker claims up to 75 minutes of runtime on the included 2.5Ah battery.

The tradeoff is that the turbo mode drains the pack quickly and returns you to full noise. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX it offers far more air and a larger platform, but it is heavier and costs more. Against the unbranded 20V blowers in this guide it has an established brand and parts support.

Ownership is easy because the 56V platform covers mowers, trimmers and other EGO tools, so extra packs are easy to buy. Keep the intake clear, store the battery partly charged and avoid leaving it in a freezing garage. Because it shares a platform with other EGO tools, it also benefits from the brand's larger packs: a 5.0Ah or larger battery extends runtime at the mid setting and makes the turbo button less necessary, which in turn keeps the noise level down for most of a session.
products.bestFor: Owners who want strong airflow they can run quietly at a lower setting.
pros: 530 CFM with a variable speed dial
Part of a large battery platform
cons: Turbo mode is loud and drains the pack

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX Cordless Leaf Blower 130 MPH 3.7 lb
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX weighs 3.7 pounds, includes a battery and charger and is described by the maker as a low-noise design. It claims up to 130 MPH air speed, which is enough to sweep dry leaves and light debris from hard surfaces like driveways, decks and garages.

The tradeoff is airflow. It does not list a CFM figure here, and a small 20V blower will struggle with wet leaves, heavy piles and large lawns. Compared with the EGO it has far less volume, but it is easier to carry and cheaper.

Store the battery indoors and keep the intake free of debris. Use it as a sweeping tool rather than a pile mover. Its light weight and modest size are the point: the battery pack is the same one that powers other 20V MAX tools in the line, so households that already own one of those tools can add the blower cheaply and keep a single charger for everything. For a postage-stamp yard, that is an advantage that bigger machines cannot match.
products.bestFor: Small yards, decks and quick driveway sweeping.

products.name: FAOGO Cordless Leaf Blower 2.8 lb With 2 Batteries
products.description:
The FAOGO is a 2.8 pound handheld blower with a turbine motor and two batteries in the box. The maker quotes more than 50 meters per second of wind speed, which is over 110 MPH, and each battery gives 13 or more minutes of strong airflow. For a patio, a car or a small porch, that is enough.

The tradeoff is runtime and capacity. Thirteen minutes of strong airflow per battery limits it to small jobs, and a turbine motor at high speed is not a quiet one, so use a lower setting. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER it is lighter but has shorter runtime.

Swap the batteries as needed and charge both after use. Keep the intake clear. With so little runtime per pack, plan the job before you begin: clear the paved edges first with the blower, then move to the lawn, and expect to finish a patio or a short driveway in one battery, which is the realistic use for a machine this light.
products.bestFor: Quick cleanups on patios, porches and cars.

products.name: LOSART 650 CFM 20V Cordless Leaf Blower 2 x 5.0Ah 4.4 lb
products.description:
The LOSART lists 650 CFM, three speed levels and two 20V 5.0Ah batteries at a weight of 4.4 pounds. The three speeds let you run low for quiet work and step up for piles. With two larger packs than most rivals, runtime is the main benefit.

The tradeoff is that CFM numbers on unbranded blowers are claims, and they are measured at the nozzle in ideal conditions. Against the EGO it offers a similar headline volume but less brand support.

Rotate the batteries and keep the intake clear. Store them indoors. With two 5.0Ah packs the kit is meant to run for hours at the low and middle settings, which is exactly how a noise-conscious owner should use it, and the three speed levels make it easy to step down as you move closer to neighboring fences.
products.bestFor: Medium yards that need long runtime on a budget.

products.name: MZK 20V Cordless Leaf Blower 600 CFM 200 MPH 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The MZK 20V blower claims up to 600 CFM and 200 MPH from a robust motor with two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger. Cordless operation lets you move freely without a cable, and the two packs allow a swap mid-job.

The tradeoff is again claims versus verified numbers. Maximum CFM and MPH are rarely sustained for long. Compared with the LOSART it offers fewer amp-hours but higher claimed speed.

Use a mid setting for daily work and reserve full speed for stubborn debris. Store batteries indoors. Because the maximum figures are quoted for the highest setting only, plan on getting noticeably less runtime when you hold the trigger wide open, and treat the second battery as the thing that makes a half-acre job possible rather than a luxury.
products.bestFor: Medium yards that want high claimed airflow.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Corded Leaf Blower 7 Amp 180 MPH 180 CFM
products.description:
The corded BLACK+DECKER offers a 7 amp motor, 180 MPH and 180 CFM, with a built-in cord retainer that stops the extension cord from pulling out mid-job. Corded power means unlimited runtime without batteries to charge.

The tradeoff is the cord and the modest airflow. At 180 CFM it moves less air than the cordless blowers here, and the cord limits where you can work.

Use a heavy-gauge extension cord rated for the amperage and keep it clear of the nozzle. A 7 amp motor draws modest current, so a standard 16 gauge cord works for runs up to about 50 feet, but anything longer needs a heavier gauge. Because there is no battery to age, this is the type of blower that tends to last the longest, and the only wear parts are the switch and the fan, which rarely fail with ordinary use.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Electric blowers are quieter than gas blowers because there is no engine, but they are not silent. A fan moving air at 150 MPH makes noise regardless of what powers it. Noise rises sharply at turbo or top speed, so the practical quiet strategy is a blower with a variable dial that lets you run at a mid setting. Published decibel figures are rare and, when given, are claims. The sound also changes character with the nozzle: a narrow concentrator nozzle raises air speed and pitch and makes the blower seem louder, while a wide flat nozzle spreads the air and sounds lower and softer. Pair a lower setting with a wide nozzle and a slow walking pace for the least intrusive result, and avoid early hours if your area restricts power equipment.

CFM measures air volume and MPH measures air speed. Moving a pile needs volume, while loosening matted leaves from pavement needs speed. The EGO lists 530 CFM, the LOSART 650 CFM and the corded BLACK+DECKER 180 CFM with 180 MPH. Both numbers are manufacturer-measured at the nozzle, so they are not comparable across brands. A blower that claims the largest volume may achieve it only at the shortest nozzle and the highest setting, which also means the shortest runtime and the most noise. Judge by what you can use all day: the mid setting that moves dry leaves across a lawn without a struggle is the figure that counts, and it is rarely printed on the box.

Voltage and amp-hours together set battery capability. The EGO's 56V platform covers many tools while the 20V blowers use smaller packs. Bare-tool listings exclude the battery, which is the expensive part. A second battery doubles runtime, which is why the LOSART and MZK kits with two packs are good value. Check that the charger is fast enough to refill one pack while you use the other, since a slow charger turns a two-battery kit into a one-battery kit. Keep both packs in rotation instead of always using the same one, so that they age evenly and neither is left drained for weeks.

The FAOGO weighs 2.8 pounds, the BLACK+DECKER 3.7 pounds and the LOSART 4.4 pounds. Lighter units are easier to hold for long jobs but may carry smaller batteries. Hold it at arm's length for a few minutes before you buy. A blower is used with a sweeping motion, so balance matters as much as weight: a battery mounted at the back counterweights the nozzle, while a front-heavy design tires the wrist. Look at the grip as well, because a thin plastic handle with no padding becomes uncomfortable within ten minutes of continuous trigger pressure.

A variable dial, as on the EGO, lets you set exactly the speed you need, while two- and three-speed switches give fewer choices. A lock-on button saves your finger on long jobs. Running at lower speed extends battery life and reduces noise. In fact the quietest habit is to use the lowest speed that works and to sweep in the same direction, so the leaves roll into a single windrow instead of being scattered and re-blown. Short, planned passes finish the job sooner than long bursts at full power and cost you far less battery and far fewer complaints from the neighbors.

A corded blower like the BLACK+DECKER 7 amp has unlimited runtime but a cord to manage. Cordless units give freedom and instant start. For a small yard near an outlet, corded is cheap and simple. For larger areas, cordless is far more practical.

specDecoder.meaning: Cubic feet per minute, a measure of air volume. Higher numbers move more material.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LOSART claims 650 and the EGO 530.

specDecoder.meaning: Air speed at the nozzle. Higher speed helps loosen stuck debris.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MZK claims 200 MPH and the BLACK+DECKER cordless 130 MPH.

specDecoder.meaning: The platform voltage. Higher voltage suits stronger tools.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO is 56V and the others are 20V class.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. More amp-hours means longer runtime.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LOSART has 5.0Ah packs and the FAOGO's packs run 13 minutes each.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared CFM and MPH claims where listed. The LOSART at 650 CFM and the EGO at 530 CFM set the top. Claims on unbranded models are treated as claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise strategy
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at variable speed, motor type and any maker noise statements. The EGO's dial and the BLACK+DECKER's low-noise design were credited. No decibel numbers are verified.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery system
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared voltage, capacity and the number of batteries. Two-pack kits scored higher for runtime. Platform support counted for the EGO.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights. The FAOGO at 2.8 pounds is the lightest. Heavier units lost points for fatigue.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand support, charger and battery care from owner feedback patterns. Established brands scored higher for parts.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER 7 amp runs without limit and has a cord retainer, but it is tied to an outlet and moves less air.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The EGO, LOSART, MZK, FAOGO and BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX give freedom and instant start. They are limited by battery capacity.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for small yards and cordless for anything bigger.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a variable dial, a lower speed that still moves dry leaves and a lock-on trigger for steady running. Keep sessions short and use a flat nozzle to sweep rather than blast.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EGO LB5302 is the best choice because you can run it at a low setting. The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is a lighter, quieter-minded alternative for small areas.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your yard is large or you have wet leaves. The EGO's airflow and platform justify the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you only sweep a patio and driveway. The BLACK+DECKER or FAOGO is enough.

maintenance.why: A clogged intake heats the motor.
Full or empty storage shortens life.

maintenance.task: Keep batteries out of freezing temperatures
maintenance.why: Cold reduces output and can damage cells.
A damaged cord is a hazard.

faq.a: Quieter than gas, yes. They still make fan noise. Running at a lower speed helps. Check local noise rules.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: It depends on the speed. The EGO claims up to 75 minutes at low speed, while the FAOGO gives about 13 minutes of strong airflow per battery.
For piles, yes. For loosening debris, speed matters. Claims on unbranded models are not comparable.
Poorly. Wet leaves weigh more and need turbo or a stronger blower. Wait for them to dry if possible.
For small yards, yes. It never runs out. For larger yards, cordless is more practical.

faq.q: Do I need a second battery?
faq.a: For anything beyond a small yard, yes. It doubles your working time.
